title: Bitcoin Near $86K as U.S. Stocks Edge Up: Live Market Update – CoinDesk
body:
Bitcoin hovered just below the $86,000 mark on Friday, while U.S. equity markets inched higher and oil prices slipped, as traders digested a confluence of macro‑economic cues and a massive options expiry on the leading crypto derivatives platform. The cryptocurrency’s resilience came amid a $14 billion wave of options contracts set to expire on Deribit, the largest single‑day expiration this year, and fresh speculation that Iran may reopen the strategic Strait of Hormuz within a week—an event that nudged West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude down to $90 a barrel.

The modest gains in the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average reflected a market cautiously optimistic after the latest jobs data showed a slight cooling in hiring, easing fears of an aggressive Federal Reserve rate hike. Yet the equity rally was muted, as investors remained wary of lingering inflation pressures and geopolitical uncertainties. In contrast, Bitcoin’s price stability suggested that the digital asset is increasingly decoupling from traditional risk‑off sentiment, finding support from a growing base of institutional participants who view it as a hedge against fiat volatility.

Deribit’s options expiration, slated for Friday, is the most consequential of the year, with contracts representing roughly $14 billion in notional value. Analysts expect the expiry to generate heightened volatility, as large positions are either settled or rolled over. “When you have that magnitude of open interest, the market can swing dramatically on a single data point or a shift in trader sentiment,” said Elena García, a senior analyst at crypto‑research firm CoinMetrics. “We’ve already seen a modest uptick in trading volume as market makers adjust their hedges, and any surprise—whether from macro data or on‑chain activity—could push Bitcoin beyond the $86,000 threshold.”

The oil market reacted to a separate, yet intertwined, set of developments. Reports that Iran could reopen the Strait of Hormuz—a critical chokepoint for roughly 20 percent of global oil shipments—within seven days sparked a brief rally in crude prices earlier in the week. However, as diplomatic channels appeared to make progress and the risk of a sudden supply disruption receded, WTI settled at $90 per barrel, down from a week‑high of $95. The decline eased pressure on energy‑sensitive sectors, contributing to the modest equity gains observed.

Meanwhile, the broader crypto ecosystem received a boost from recent activity at Ledn, a crypto‑backed lending platform co‑founded by Mauricio Di Bartolomeo. Ledn has now originated more than $10 billion in loans, underscoring the growing appetite for crypto‑linked credit products among both retail and institutional borrowers. Di Bartolomeo highlighted that the platform’s expansion is being driven by “greater confidence in digital assets as collateral” and a “maturing regulatory environment” that is attracting traditional finance players to the space.

Looking ahead, market participants will be watching several key indicators. The Federal Reserve’s upcoming policy meeting could set the tone for equity markets and, by extension, risk appetite for cryptocurrencies. On the crypto side, the outcome of Deribit’s options expiry will likely dictate short‑term price dynamics for Bitcoin and other major tokens. Additionally, any concrete developments regarding the Strait of Hormuz—whether a reopening or renewed tensions—could reignite oil price volatility, with spillover effects on both equities and digital assets.

In sum, Bitcoin’s near‑$86,000 price point reflects a market at a crossroads, balancing institutional confidence against a backdrop of macro‑economic and geopolitical flux. As the week unfolds, the interplay between a massive derivatives expiry, evolving oil supply outlook, and central bank policy will shape the trajectory of both traditional and crypto markets, setting the stage for the next phase of price action.
